title: Stability bringup sprintlet log and telemetry spikeplan
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact field notebook for a short (2–3 day) stability bringup during a tight sprintlet. The goal: exercise rollout gating, validate new traffic-phasing curves, and tune telemetry spike thresholds without a full-scale canary.

Context:
- Target release: runtime v2.7.1 (small perf/kv-cache change + batching tweak)
- Motivation: reduce 95th latency regression observed in nightly perf sims; validate throttle and backoff on warm start paths.
- Risk profile: medium — changes touch batch scheduler and kv-cache lifecycling. No schema or client-side contract changes.

Quick checklist (preflight, to complete at least 48h before start):
- [ ] Merge green on PRs (see linked PR), tag release candidate and create release branch ENG-4123-rc1
- [ ] Smoke tests updated and run locally: smoke/basic-gen, smoke/kv-warm, smoke/cache-invalidate
- [ ] Observability: ensure new metrics are emitted (batch_queue_depth, kv_warm_ratio, cold_start_count) and dashboards provisioned
- [ ] Run synthetic load for 1h at baseline to capture pre-change telemetry snapshot (window: 2026-11-09 09:00–10:00 UTC)
- [ ] Notify SRE and Support: post schedule in #release-ops and add on-call rotation for 12–24h after rollout

Mini rollout calendar (48-hour sprintlet):
Day 0 — Prep and dry-run (08:00–16:00 UTC)
- 08:00: Kickoff (15m) — owners: Priya, Ethan. Confirm signatures.
- 09:00–12:00: Dry-run on staging with 50% synthetic latency mix; exercise long-tail paths (large seq lengths). Capture metrics.
- 13:00–15:00: Adjust throttle curve if batch_queue_depth exceeds 80th percentile forecast. Document change.
- 15:30: Readout and go/no-go decision for Day 1.

Day 1 — Micro-canary (09:00–18:00 UTC)
- 09:00: Promote rc1 to micro-canary lane (2% global traffic, region-limited to us-west1).
- 09:05–10:00: Run smoke suite against canary. Verify correctness and no crash loops.
- 10:00–12:00: Observe telemetry; specific thresholds: 95th latency < baseline+8%, error rate < 0.05%
- 12:00: If pass, ramp to 10% traffic; otherwise roll back to previous RC and start incident drill.
- 14:00–18:00: Keep at 10% while exercising heavy KV-warm scenarios.

Day 2 — Broadening and wrap (08:00–16:00 UTC)
- 08:00: If metrics stable, ramp to 40% and expand to eu-west1.
- 12:00: Final validation run; if fine, schedule full rollout overnight (quiet window pref 02:00–06:00 local TZ) or adopt canary-as-prod for next 24h.

Telemetry & alert tuning (what to watch):
- Primary signals (auto-collected):
  - p50/p90/p95 latency per route and per model variant
  - 1m/5m error rate (5xx, 4xx spikes)
  - batch_queue_depth (per-worker) — alert if sustained above configured 95th
  - kv_warm_ratio (proportion of requests served from KV warmed cache) — regressions indicate cache thrash
  - cold_start_count — correlate with elevated latency spikes
- Derived heuristics:
  - If p95 increases > 12% for 30m with concurrent batch_queue_depth rise, restrict batch formation (decrease max batch size) and enable temporary per-route safety lanes
  - If kv_warm_ratio drops > 15% while request variance unchanged, run targeted cache-warm job and hold rollout progression

Staffing & roles (short rotation):
- Release lead: Priya Natarajan — overall decision authority
- Observability lead: Ethan Park — dashboards, alerts, immediate telemetry triage
- Patch owner (rollback author): Marta Ruiz — prepares rollback, hotfix branch, and coord with release lead
- On-call SRE: (rotate) — responder for infra-level incidents
- Support liaison: Liam O'Connor — customer comms and internal triage notes

Smoke test matrix (quick runbook):
- smoke/basic-gen: generate small/medium/long sequences, assert output steady and no OOM
- smoke/kv-warm: exercise repeated requests to same contexts and assert kv_warm_ratio >= 80% after warm-up window
- smoke/cache-invalidate: run invalidate sequence and confirm subsequent cold_start_count spikes then returns to baseline after warm job
- smoke/throughput-burst: run 120s burst at 2x baseline to observe backpressure behavior (watch batch_queue_depth and worker cpu)

Rollback / quick recovery steps (for micro-canary):
- Triage: if any fatal signal (crashloop, error spike > 1% or p95 > baseline+25%), immediately pause routing to micro-canary lane (API: routing/weight set 0)
- Invoke rollback: patch owner merges revert-hotfix branch and promotes previous build to the lane (document PR id)
- Post-rollback: collect telemetry snapshot for 30m, open incident ticket ENG-4123-RB-YYYYMMDD, assign SRE and release lead for postmortem

Go/no-go decision rubric (explicit):
- Must pass: smoke suite fully green; no regressions on p95 above +8%; error rate within 2x pre-change jitter baseline
- May proceed with caution: minor p95 blips that self-resolve within 15m and are not accompanied by error spikes or CPU saturations
- Must abort: sustained regressions > 15% p95, error spike > 0.5%, or any crashlooping pods

Communication plan (short):
- Preflight: announce schedule and key contacts in #release-ops and to SRE paging email list 24h prior
- During: rolling updates to thread in #release-ops, once per major step (canary start, ramp to 10%, ramp to 40%, final) with short telemetry snapshot (p95, errors, batch depth)
- Post: write quick release note in Confluence and paste summary to #release-ops and customer-success if there are customer-facing changes

Known unknowns & open questions (to resolve before dry-run):
- What is acceptable transient p95 uplift for long-sequence routes? (action: tag product for decision)
- Need an owner for the cross-region warm job — suggest infra-runner team; pinged Marta
- Do we have synthetic scenarios that mimic cross-tenant KV eviction patterns? If not, schedule a small generator run (ENG-4123-synth-1)

Post-rollout follow-up (tasks for 72h after full ramp):
- 24h: stability digest (lead) — collect and annotate any new alerts, customer issues
- 48h: if stable, merge rc into main and bump chart version; close ENG-4123-rc1
- 72h: retro notes and a short postmortem if any mitigation was performed

Notes to self: keep the micro-canary lane intentionally small and region-limited. This sprintlet is for surfaces only — if we see system-wide surprises, escalate and halt the big rollout.
